purpose: Make the REX ledger an active reusable checklist for recurring and persistent problems before and after every measured task.

recurrence_levels.NEW: first observed occurrence; bind event and immediate disposition
recurrence_levels.RECURRING: same REX on >=2 distinct task_id or run_id; add or strengthen automated prevention/checklist
recurrence_levels.PERSISTENT: same REX on >=3 distinct tasks or >=2 distinct missions, or recurrence after an accepted preventive control; force architecture/resource/role review
recurrence_levels.REGRESSION: reappears after CONTROL/closure; reopen REX, block relevant CONTROL claim and create first-red action

before_task: mission_id task_id assignment_id crew_id and state use registered namespaces
entity action status and lifecycle state are not overloaded
new namespace has a declared owner
if_triggered: repair registry or state machine before adding automation

before_task: new mission task role evidence and status terms are registered or explicitly provisional
proof_of_prevention: no unregistered term in emitted receipt

checklist.problem: YAML line length / recurring formatting CI defect
before_task: changed YAML is linted before merge
generated YAML obeys bounded formatting rules
if_triggered: repair generator or lint rule instead of repeated manual patch

before_task: active assignment is current for this mission
if_triggered: do not count stale queue as current load

before_task: victory condition and DoV are named
promotion authority is explicit and bounded
if_triggered: require independent or merged-head repeat where applicable

before_task: workflow existence is not treated as runtime evidence
runner/job telemetry will capture actual execution
if_triggered: do not patch application code before runner assignment unless separate evidence justifies it
proof_of_prevention: runtime receipt bound to exact SHA

allocation_rules: persistent or regression REX affecting a competency adds reverse pressure against assigning the same unsupported crew/resource pattern
successful preventive-control repeats add positive evidence to the responsible crew competency but never auto-promote a role
PCA features may include REX recurrence and prevention-success counts only when sourced from measured task receipts
BT pairwise outcomes may compare allocation strategies on REX recurrence only for comparable task classes
